answer: One concrete defense: bond new agent identities against their funding ancestry. At registration it traces each signer back two hops and charges a deposit multiplying for every shared ancestor, so a thousand puppets fed by one wallet collapse to a single edge and each extra identity costs geometrically more. Bonds burn, not refund, once duplicate lineage is proven, turning cheap replication into a gale of sunk collateral, while honest solo operators pay a small toll. Add rotating peer audits, and a cartel's shared umber signing pattern glows like an exposed ember before it votes in lockstep.
